Which of the following statement(s) is/are incorrect?
a. Communist Party leaders worked for the Visalandhra Movement and propagated the concept of Visalandhra even before the formation of 'Andhra State. aye
b. Communists became a great force in Telangana polities. fais oc. Communists opposed the formation of integrated linguistic States
x:
Statement (a) is correct. The Communist Party strongly supported the demand for Visalandhra, advocating the unification of all Telugu-speaking areas into a single linguistic state even before the formation of Andhra State in 1953. Communist leaders regarded linguistic states as a means of strengthening democratic administration and promoting regional development. Statement (b) is correct. The Communists emerged as a powerful political force in Telangana, particularly during the Telangana Armed Struggle (1946–1951) against the feudal system under the Nizam. Their leadership among peasants and agricultural labourers gave them significant political influence in the region. Statement (c) is incorrect. The Communist Party did not oppose the formation of integrated linguistic states. On the contrary, it consistently supported the creation of linguistic states and strongly advocated the formation of Visalandhra by merging Andhra State with the Telugu-speaking districts of Hyderabad State.
Therefore, only Statement (c) is incorrect.
Hence, the correct answer is
Option (4).
n: Communist Party – Strong supporter of Visalandhra.

s: The Justice Party Government in Madras Presidency helped the enactment of legislation for the formation of which University?
The Justice Party Government helped in the historic formation of which University?
Justice Party Government helped the formation of which University?
x:
The Justice Party Government in the Madras Presidency played a significant role in the establishment of Andhra University, the first university created primarily to meet the higher educational needs of the Telugu-speaking people. Before its establishment, students from the Andhra region had to depend largely on the University of Madras for higher education. The growing demand for a separate university gained momentum through the efforts of Telugu intellectuals, educationists and public leaders. Responding to these demands, the Andhra University Act was passed in 1925, and the University was formally established in 1926. Initially, the University functioned from Bezwada (Vijayawada) and was later shifted to Waltair (Visakhapatnam), where it continues to be one of the premier educational institutions in the country.
Hence, the correct answer is
Option (2).
n: Andhra University Act – 1925
Established – 1926
First Vice-Chancellor – Dr. C. R. Reddy
Present Headquarters – Visakhapatnam

Arrange the following former Chief Ministers of Andhra Pradesh in chronological order:
A. Tanguturi Anjaiah
B. Damodaram Sanjivayya
C. P.V. Narasimha Rao
D. Kasu Brahmananda Reddy
x:
Damodaram Sanjivayya became the Chief Minister of Andhra Pradesh in 1960, becoming the first Dalit Chief Minister of any Indian State. He was succeeded by Kasu Brahmananda Reddy, who served from 1964 to 1971 and had one of the longest tenures as Chief Minister. P. V. Narasimha Rao became the Chief Minister in 1971 and later went on to become the Prime Minister of India (1991–1996). Tanguturi Anjaiah assumed office in 1980 and is remembered for introducing several labour welfare measures.
Thus, the chronological order is: Damodaram Sanjivayya → Kasu Brahmananda Reddy → P. V. Narasimha Rao → Tanguturi Anjaiah
Hence, the correct answer is
Option (2).
n: Damodaram Sanjivayya – First Dalit Chief Minister in India.
P. V. Narasimha Rao – Only Prime Minister from Andhra Pradesh.

s: During whose reign did N. T. Rama Rao establish the Telugu Desam Party?
x:
The Telugu Desam Party (TDP) was founded by Nandamuri Taraka Rama Rao (N. T. Rama Rao) on 29 March 1982 with the objective of protecting Telugu self-respect (Telugu Atma Gauravam) and providing an alternative to the Congress Party. At the time of the party's formation, Bhavanam Venkatarami Reddy was the Chief Minister of Andhra Pradesh. He served as Chief Minister from 24 February 1982 to 20 September 1982. Within a short period of its formation, the Telugu Desam Party achieved a historic victory in the 1983 Andhra Pradesh Assembly Elections, bringing N. T. Rama Rao to power.
Hence, the correct answer is
Option (3).

Founder – N. T. Rama Rao
Chief Minister at that time – Bhavanam Venkatarami Reddy

s: When was the Gentlemen's Agreement signed?
x:
The Gentlemen's Agreement was signed on 20 February 1956 between the leaders of Andhra State and Telangana. The agreement provided safeguards for Telangana regarding employment, education, expenditure and political representation before the formation of Andhra Pradesh on 1 November 1956.
Hence, the correct answer is
Option (3).
n: Gentlemen's Agreement – 20 February 1956 The 1956 Gentlemen's Agreement was signed by 8 key political leaders representing the Andhra and Telangana regions on February 20, 1956, to safeguard Telangana's interests prior to the formation of unified Andhra Pradesh. Signatories from Andhra Region
Bezwada Gopal Reddy – Chief Minister of Andhra State
Neelam Sanjeeva Reddy – Andhra Congress leader (later Chief Minister and President of India)
Gouthu Latchanna – Andhra leader and minister
Alluri Satyanarayana Raju – Andhra Congress committee leader Signatories from Telangana (Hyderabad State) Region
Burgula Ramakrishna Rao – Chief Minister of Hyderabad State
K. V. Ranga Reddy – Telangana political leader
Marri Channa Reddy – Telangana leader (later Chief Minister of undivided AP)
J. V. Narasing Rao The key provisions ensured financial protection, job security, and regional autonomy for Telangana. Finances and Development
Surplus Revenue: Extra money earned from the Telangana region must be spent only on the development of Telangana.
Shared Expenses: State administration costs were to be split proportionally between the two regions. Jobs and Education
Mulki Rules: Local job and education rules were kept, meaning only people who lived in Telangana for a set time could get local government jobs.
Educational Safeguards: School and college seats in Telangana were reserved for students from Telangana. Governance and Power
Regional Committee: A special committee of Telangana assembly members was formed to look after regional development, planning, and local rules.
Cabinet Balance: The state cabinet was to have a fair number of ministers from both the Telangana and Andhra regions.
The Actual Ratio: The official Gentlemen's Agreement of 1956 stipulated a 60:40 ratio for Cabinet representation.

The Distribution: This mandated that 60% of the cabinet ministers were to be from the Andhra region and 40% from the Telangana region, reflecting the respective population and assembly sizes at the time.
The Leadership Rule: If the Chief Minister was chosen from Andhra, the Deputy Chief Minister position had to go to a leader from Telangana, and vice versa
